# Dubickas (2009): complexity of integer sequences generated by linear maps

## Citation

Artūras Dubickas, *On integer sequences generated by linear maps*,
Glasgow Mathematical Journal **51**(2), 243–252 (2009).
[Publisher DOI and primary article](https://doi.org/10.1017/S0017089508004655).

## What we use

Theorem 5 (p. 246) and its proof in section 5 (pp. 249–250) are a primary
antecedent for the parity-factor complexity method. Equal finite
parity strings force a large power of two to divide the difference
between their starting states; an upper growth bound and pigeonhole
then constrain low factor complexity. Its stated application is to
a divergent positive `3x+1` trajectory.

The [one-edit mechanical denominator law](../areas/cycles/results/one-edit-mechanical-denominator-growth/README.md)
uses the existing odd-only repeated-factor version, retains the
denominator of a primitive cycle, and proves every step it needs.
No result from this paper is an additional proof assumption.

## How it is checked

The primary publisher PDF's Theorem 5 and proof were read on
2026-11-08, and the finite congruence and growth mechanism were
rederived. The paper is cited for antecedence; it is not presented
as a new repository formalization or a replay of the full article.
